text: Confirmed from here, through Google's and Cloudflare's public resolvers: join.face.spirit.andyflinn.com and a made-up xyz.face.spirit.andyflinn.com both resolve to 194.37.81.237, the same address as spirit.andyflinn.com, so the wildcard works. The bare face.spirit.andyflinn.com already answers at Cloudflare; Google is still holding its earlier 'no such name' and will catch up within the hour. DNS is done. Next is the Caddy setup on the VPS (the ask above), then issue 2.

Yes, mostly. Asked directly just now, all three DreamHost name servers answer the WILDCARD: join.face.spirit.andyflinn.com gives 194.37.81.237, the same machine as spirit.andyflinn.com. The bare face.spirit.andyflinn.com answered once, a few minutes ago, and right now says 'not found' on all three, so DreamHost is probably still settling. It's the less important of the two: every app and user name is under the wildcard, and the bare name only needs to show a 'no name here' page. Public resolvers still hold the earlier 'not found' for a while (my machine does). I'll look at the bare one again later.

Yes. It's a setting on your node, and its default is 'face' in front of your relay's domain: face.spirit.andyflinn.com. Change it there and your node reads names against the new one. DNS and the Caddy block then have to name the same thing, since those two are set by hand.

Yes, as ruled (G17, THE ROUTE): a setting on the owner node, default 'face' in front of the relay's domain, so face.spirit.andyflinn.com here, and changeable. In code today only half exists: faceRoute.nameOf takes the face domain as an argument (faceRoute.js:34). The setting itself, where the owner node stores it and hands it to appFaceApp, isn't built yet; it comes with claude-windows' wiring.

Issue 2 of 3: letting appFaceApp reach join. When a visitor asks for join.face.spirit.andyflinn.com, the request ends up at appFaceApp on your node, which knows 'join' is yours. It then has to hand the request to join's program, running on the same box. It can't today, on purpose: an app like appFaceApp may only look inside its own folder, and it holds no keys. The proposal: give appFaceApp one extra ability, 'send this request to the app called join on this box and give me its answer'. Your node does the actual reaching, and appFaceApp never learns the address. Only an app whose manifest says it needs this gets it, and your node still reaches only apps on its own box that have said they serve visitors. Go! = give appFaceApp that one ability. (Issue 1's last step, writing the Caddy setup for the VPS into bash/, I'll bring back as one line after issue 3.)

Yes, simple, and that's exactly the route as ruled: ask your box once, cache in RAM, forward to join's owner, and never ask again for join. Issue 2 is only the very last step, after that forward. join's owner is your box, so the visitor's request arrives at your node saying 'this is for join'. Your node still has to pass it to join's program, which runs beside it on the same box as a separate process. That hand-over is what's missing today. The ability I asked about is just that: your node passing a request for 'join' to the join program next to it, and bringing back the answer. If you'd rather the node do that itself, with no app involved, that's even simpler, and the same Go! covers it.

DNS settled: all three DreamHost name servers now answer both records. face.spirit.andyflinn.com and *.face.spirit.andyflinn.com (tested with join.face.spirit) both give 194.37.81.237. The DNS half of step 1 is done; what remains there is Caddy's one wildcard block and its certificate.

Understood, and it takes issue 2 off the table: no new ability for appFaceApp. For now your box only answers the route question truthfully: 'I am the owner of join', or 'not the owner, it's <key>', or 'nobody has that name'. The VPS caches that and forwards. A request that reaches your node for a name you own gets a plain named answer, 'not served yet', until the rules for server processes are settled. Those rules become their own design row: app-server processes run inside the SpiritOS process subsystem (spirit/run/process/...), started and watched like any other process, and how your node hands them a request comes out of that. Go! = I build the route answer and the VPS's cache-and-forward as described, and put 'server processes in the process subsystem' on the board as a design row for us to discuss. Then issue 3.

Agreed, which is why it gets its own design row rather than being decided in passing here. Nothing gets built on it until we've discussed it: what the process type is, how it's started and watched, and how it receives a request. The route work stops short of it, at 'not served yet'.

Starting step 1 (browser to the subdomain's owner and back, answered 'not served yet' at your box). Two small things appFaceApp on your node lacks, one of them your gate. (1) ITS OWN NODE'S KEY. To answer 'I'm the owner of join', it must compare the grant row with its own node's public key, and a booted app isn't told that today. The key is public anyway, since every node's card answers it, but adding self() to what a booted app is handed widens that interface, so it's yours: Go or No. (2) THE FACE DOMAIN. A booted app can't read relays.json to derive the default, so the setting lives in appFaceApp's own folder (face-domain.json, next to grants.json), written at setup to face.spirit.andyflinn.com and changeable there. That one is plumbing and needs no gate. Go! = api.self() returning the node's public key, and nothing else.
